posts.heading: November 4, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to 24 species, 15 seen and 18 heard, with 279 feeder visits, well above the past week's average of 174.6 visits and the second-highest visit count of the eight days. Species count was also above the 21.6 average, while heard detections (130) ran well below the average of 300.6. Tufted Titmouse led the visits with 117 and Carolina Chickadee followed with 66, while Carolina Wren (19), Northern Cardinal (11) and House Finch (9) also made regular visits.

The Northern Flicker returned after 10 days away, last recorded on 2026-10-25, with one probable visual. Eleven species were recorded on all seven days, including today, and Red-shouldered Hawk and White-throated Sparrow were recorded on six of the seven. Northern Mockingbird and Red-bellied Woodpecker, both recorded on each of the previous seven days, were not recorded today.

There was no first confident visual record and no species heard for the first time at this station. The audio source changed repeatedly between 06:32 and 07:24 and again between 17:04 and 17:05. The first visual was a Carolina Chickadee 2 min before sunrise, and the last was a Carolina Wren 22 min before sunset.

posts.heading: November 3, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to 22 species, with 19 heard and 10 seen, 61 feeder visits, and 221 heard detections. That was quieter than the past week: visits sat well below the weekly average of 182.4, and detections were below the average of 322.9, while the species count of 22 was close to the average of 21.0. The first visual was a Chipping Sparrow 48 min after sunrise, and the last was a Carolina Chickadee 47 min before sunset.

All 13 species recorded on every day of the past week were present today, including Tufted Titmice with 22 confident visual visits and Carolina Chickadees with 14. White-throated Sparrow, recorded on 6 of the 7 days, was heard 30 times. Brown-headed Cowbird, Cedar Waxwing, Golden-crowned Kinglet, Gray Catbird, Common Grackle, and Hairy Woodpecker, which were recorded on other days of the week, were not recorded today.

No species was seen or heard for the first time at the station today. The audio source was changed many times throughout the day, beginning at 05:30 and continuing through 22:02, so heard detections came from more than one source. These changes are logged as the only station change for the day and do not by themselves account for the lower totals.

posts.heading: November 2, 2026
posts.text:
Across November 2, the station logged 17 species, 17 heard and 7 seen, with 75 feeder visits. That is below the seven-day average of 21.6 species and 196.3 visits, and detections of 290 sit below the average of 334.0. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees led the detections, with 61 and 59, and Tufted Titmice also led the visits with 30 confident sightings. Carolina Chickadee, Carolina Wren, Blue Jay, Northern Cardinal, and Eastern Phoebe were all recorded on each of the last seven days, including this one, while White-throated Sparrow, Brown-headed Cowbird, and Red-shouldered Hawk were not recorded today.

The station's audio source was switched many times over the past week, most heavily on October 27 and 28, and it also changed on this day, so detections from those periods come from different microphones. The day's first visual was a Carolina Chickadee and its last was a Carolina Wren. No species was heard here for the first time, and no first confident visual record was made.

The audio source changed repeatedly through the early morning of November 2, and the visit count on November 1 was 403, well above any other day in the window. Today's visit total of 75 came after that unusually busy day.
